the panel makes discrete judgments on external outcomes","Latent factor models require large N for stable covariance; a panel of non-experts is typically small, so noise cancellation is weaker"],"overturn_conditions":["If the questionnaire analogy holds, removing checklist items that load on the task-relevant factor should disproportionately reduce panel reliability; if reliability is unaffected, the items are not driving the gain."],"shared_structure":["Decomposition of a complex judgment into measurable sub-components (items / ICs)","Aggregation across independent noisy estimators (panelists / modes) to cancel error","Validity anchored in a generating function (task ground truth / linear latent factor)"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a questionnaire's reliability requires that items load on a common latent factor, a checklist's reliability gain requires that items jointly track the task's generating variables.","If panelist judgments split into multiple uncorrelated factors (e.g., a 'checklist-compliance' factor and a 'task-discrimination' factor), the gain is factor-dependent, not holistic."]},"claim":"A panel of non-experts with an explicit checklist produces more reliable judgments because the checklist decomposes a high-validity task into measurable sub-proxies; aggregation then cancels residual per-item noise, while the expert's intuition integrates untestable confounders (affect, coherence bias) that degrade calibration.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If panelists are merely copying a visible consensus rather than voting independently, aggregation provides no noise cancellation and reliability collapses to the first voter.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist items are the result of the designer's intuition and the task base rate is extreme (e.g., 99% negative), the panel may exhibit 'checklist compliance' by vacuously marking all items as present without discriminating, matching the base rate without a reliability gain.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task requires cross-item integration (e.g., Gestalt pattern recognition, multi-step deductive dependencies), decomposing it into independent checklist items may destroy structural information, and the expert's holistic intuition may outperform.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal path: Objectively verifiable outcome \u2192 checklist items proxy the true generating variables \u2192 each panelist samples the proxies with bounded, roughly independent error \u2192 majority aggregation cancels noise \u2192 higher calibration than single-shot intuition. The 'reliability gain' is causal because it is mediated by the checklist's *proxy validity*: if the items are re-derived from a different orthogonal sample of the same task and still predict, the gain is not a chance tracking artifact.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
